quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What should you do when driving in a construction zone?

options.text: Speed up a little.
Be ready for anything unusual.
Expect construction workers to let you pass first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for anything unusual.
questions.explanation: Construction zones can have unexpected hazards. Drive slowly and carefully to protect yourself, other drivers, and construction workers.

questions.question: When traffic is moving at 50 to 55 mph, you will have the fewest accidents if you:

options.text: Drive a few miles per hour faster than other vehicles.
Stay at the same speed as the traffic around you.
Drive a few miles per hour slower than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay at the same speed as the traffic around you.
questions.explanation: Drive at the same speed as other traffic. Vehicles moving at the same speed in the same direction cannot hit each other. Crashes happen when vehicles travel at different speeds.

questions.question: What does this yellow pennant-shaped sign mean?

options.text: Right turns only.
Right turns allowed.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: Yellow pennant signs warn drivers that passing is not allowed in this area.

questions.question: What does a red painted curb mean?

options.text: Loading zone.
Pick up or drop off passengers only.
No parking, standing, or stopping allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking, standing, or stopping allowed.
questions.explanation: You cannot park, stop, or stand at a red curb.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic light ahead.
Stop.
Yield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic light ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic light is coming up.

questions.question: What does a steady red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: You cannot turn in the direction the arrow points.
You can turn in that direction after stopping completely.
You can turn in that direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you cannot go in that direction. Stop and wait for a green signal before turning.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash.
You need more space between cars when driving faster.
Both A and B.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B.
questions.explanation: Faster speeds make crashes more deadly. At speeds over 80 mph, survival is unlikely. Higher speeds also mean you need more distance to stop, so keep more space between your car and others.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians crossing.
School crossing.
Jogging path.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians crossing.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert drivers to watch for people crossing the road. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Know you are driving the wrong way.
Treat it like a stop sign.
Wait until it turns green.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, look for other traffic and pedestrians, and then proceed safely.

questions.question: When can you drive off the road to pass another vehicle?

options.text: When the car ahead is turning left.
When there are two or more lanes in your direction.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never drive onto the shoulder or off the paved road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: You should drive on the shoulder to pass a car:

options.text: If the vehicle ahead is turning left.
Never.
If the shoulder is wide enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never pass another vehicle on the shoulder. The other driver will not expect you to be there. They may pull off the road and hit you.

questions.question: You must show proof of insurance to law enforcement:

options.text: Only if you are in a collision.
If you are in a collision or get a traffic ticket.
Only if you get a traffic ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in a collision or get a traffic ticket.
questions.explanation: You must carry proof of insurance when you drive. Show your insurance proof and license to a police officer whenever asked after a traffic stop or collision.

questions.question: The driver ahead stops at a crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Slowly pass at 10 mph or less.
Stop and wait for all pedestrians to cross.
Change lanes, look, and pass the stopped vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for all pedestrians to cross.
questions.explanation: Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. Pedestrians you cannot see may be crossing. Stop and move only after all pedestrians have crossed.

questions.question: Yellow lines separate:

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions.
All carpool lanes from regular lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of a road used for two-way traffic. A solid yellow line means do not pass. A broken yellow line means you may pass if it is safe.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, it is safe to move back to the right lane:

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You can return to your lane when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror. Always check your blind spots before moving back.

questions.question: Driving at night is more dangerous than driving during the day because:

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead.
The road is always more slippery.
Your reaction time is slower.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead because of poor lighting and glare from oncoming headlights. Use your headlights and drive carefully in the dark.

questions.question: Construction zone signs are usually:

options.text: Square or rectangular with white and red colors.
Round or octagonal with black and yellow colors.
Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black colors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black colors.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs have an orange background with black letters or symbols. They are placed on the right side of the road, or on both sides for divided highways.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is:

options.text: Allowed from the side with the solid yellow line.
Not allowed from either side.
Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: When a solid yellow line is next to a broken yellow line, passing is allowed only from the side with the broken line.

questions.question: A broken yellow line between two lanes of traffic means:

options.text: Both lanes are going in the same direction.
Passing is allowed when safe.
Passing is not allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed when safe.
questions.explanation: A dashed yellow line separates lanes with traffic going in opposite directions. You may pass when there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver:

options.text: Stay calm and focus on driving.
Drive faster than the speed limit.
Tailgate other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and focus on driving.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, stay calm and focus on the road. Do not take other drivers' actions personally. Leave plenty of time for your trip, follow speed limits, and be patient with other drivers.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, you should drive:

options.text: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
At the legal speed limit.
Slower than freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Enter the freeway at or near the speed of traffic, unless traffic is going faster than the legal speed limit.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, you should drive:

options.text: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
5 to 10 mph slower than freeway traffic.
At the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging onto a freeway, enter at or near the speed of traffic.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Watch for people crossing your path.
No passing zone.
Work zone ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This orange warning sign tells you that roadwork is ahead. Stay alert for temporary traffic control signs in work zones.

questions.question: To enter a gap in highway traffic:

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and let other vehicles move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, make sure no vehicles are in your way. Always check traffic to the side and behind your vehicle.

questions.question: As of August 1, 2008, what is the nighttime curfew for 16- and 17-year-old drivers?

options.text: 10 p.m. to 6 a.m.
11 p.m. to 5 a.m.
12 a.m. to 5 a.m.

questions.correctAnswerText: 11 p.m. to 5 a.m.
questions.explanation: 16- and 17-year-old drivers cannot drive between 11 p.m. and 5 a.m., unless driving for work, school, religious activities, medical needs, or as part of the Safe Ride Program.
